observed.limits: The retained output identifies one socket timeout but provides no request route, request identifier, individual timed-out duration, response body, or causal runtime trace. Completed-request latency statistics do not describe the timed-out request.

source_evidence.fact: Uses a SQLite connection string containing the supplied database path, with no explicit request-pool or writer-queue configuration in this setup.
Each request gets a SqliteConnection through Db.Connect; source comments describe provider connection pooling.
GET /feed and GET /posts/{id} await Dapper SQLite queries on request-scoped connections.
POST /posts and POST /posts/{id}/like execute SQLite INSERT operations on request-scoped connections without an explicit application-level writer queue.
The author documents default thread-pool/runtime settings and no extra SQLite pragmas.

The author separately describes historical long-tail latency and proposes SQLite lock waits blocking worker threads and thread-pool starvation, explicitly saying the hypothesis was not verified. Historical capacity figures are not current-trial evidence.
All candidates use the same wrk invocation with no per-case timeout override.

hypotheses.mechanism: SQLite write contention or blocking provider work combined with default .NET thread-pool scheduling could queue an occasional request long enough for wrk to time out.
hypotheses.support: Request-scoped pooled connections and concurrent SQLite INSERT paths in source; elevated completion tail latency; CPU below the one-core budget; author independently identifies this as an unverified design concern.
hypotheses.confidence: Plausible, not established by retained evidence. Async provider internals and actual thread-pool queue state were not traced. Total process threads increasing 17 to 29 is not a thread-pool-specific measurement.

hypotheses.mechanism: A transient storage/fsync, runtime pause or scheduler delay could also produce one isolated timeout.
hypotheses.confidence: Possible alternatives only; no per-request disk, GC, scheduling, or lock traces identify the cause.

conclusion.http_status_for_timed_out_request: unknown; no non-2xx/non-3xx responses were recorded
conclusion.classification: Keep measured_with_errors and exclude from the zero-error ranking. Trial 3 should run unchanged; a clean later trial does not erase the recorded trial-2 timeout.
